policy_trace.observation: R66 _get_owned_docs_canvas_or_error compares the earliest audit row creator with current_user.id and is used by get/update.
R66 _get_owned_email_canvas_or_error compares the earliest audit row creator with current_user.id and is used by get/send.
PdfCanvasService._require_owner checks canvas owner before content mutations.
Authentication only at router level; GET has no current_user; update_cell/add_chart pass current_user.id but no owner check is applied to the existing canvas.
Queries CanvasAudit by canvas_id + canvas_type only; user_id is stored on the new row but not compared with the existing canvas owner.
Routes pass current_user.id but the underlying queries use canvas_id + canvas_type only.
Same unscoped CanvasAudit query; user_id is only the new row author.
CanvasAudit carries user_id/tenant_id and Canvas carries created_by/tenant_id/workspace_id, so per-user authority is representable; single-tenant does not remove it.

conclusion: On frozen f5a2413ce, a different active same-tenant authenticated user was able to read the owner's sheets and coding canvases, append owner-canvas rows, and create a same-canvas_id row that changed the owner's subsequent read. The inactive actor was refused with zero effect, and supplied body user_id was not authority. This reproduces WO-WEB-CANVAS-AUTHORITY-01 at the public ASGI route/service/SQL boundary. It is not a repair, acceptance or app-completion claim.
